root_cause.text: The arm64 BPF JIT allocator requested only 4-byte alignment for the JIT buffer, so `build_plt()` could place `struct bpf_plt::target` (a `u64` updated concurrently by `bpf_arch_text_poke()`) at a misaligned address, enabling torn 64-bit reads/stores and atomicity violations.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc(image_size, &ro_image_ptr, sizeof(u32), ...)` to `sizeof(u64)`, and the commit message states that a 4-byte-aligned base address could make `build_plt()` fail to align `target` on an 8-byte boundary, causing UBSAN misaligned-access warnings and risking torn reads during `WRITE_ONCE()`/`ldr` access.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adjust the BPF JIT binary pack allocation to use 64-bit alignment instead of 32-bit alignment.
intent_record.what: In bpf_int_jit_compile(), the third argument passed to bpf_jit_binary_pack_alloc() was changed from sizeof(u32) to sizeof(u64) while keeping the rest of the call unchanged.
intent_record.how: This changes the alignment or allocation granularity requested for the JIT binary pack from 4 bytes to 8 bytes, which can affect how the generated BPF image and associated metadata are laid out in memory and help satisfy 64-bit alignment requirements at runtime.

grouping_result.intent: Adjust the BPF JIT binary pack allocation to use 64-bit alignment instead of 32-bit alignment.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by increasing the BPF JIT allocator alignment from 4-byte/32-bit to 8-byte/64-bit, preventing misaligned placement of the 64-bit PLT target field and the resulting torn accesses.

candidates.rationale: This line requests only 4-byte alignment for the JIT buffer allocation. That allows the PLT area to be placed at a misaligned address, so the 64-bit bpf_plt::target field can be accessed non-atomically during concurrent text pokes.

vuln_statements.explanation: This allocation request uses only 4-byte alignment for the JIT buffer, which can misalign the PLT region and place struct bpf_plt::target at an address that is not 8-byte aligned, enabling torn 64-bit accesses during concurrent bpf_arch_text_poke() updates.

    arm64: eBPF JIT compiler
    
    The JIT compiler emits A64 instructions. It supports eBPF only.
    Legacy BPF is supported thanks to conversion by BPF core.
    
    JIT is enabled in the same way as for other architectures:
    
            echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/core/bpf_jit_enable
    
    Or for additional compiler output:
    
            echo 2 > /proc/sys
